# Engineering Tutorial: Designing a Reliable Request-Processing Service

## 1. Introduction

In modern distributed systems, reliability is not a feature—it is a prerequisite. A service that ingests requests, validates them, processes the underlying work, and gracefully handles failures must be designed with explicit assumptions about partial failure, network partitions, and resource exhaustion. This tutorial walks through the end-to-end design of a **Reliable Request-Processing Service (RRPS)**. We will cover architecture, component responsibilities, failure modes, observability, testing strategies, and concrete code examples.
